2  THIS CCC IS FILED UNDER ARTICLE 215 R/W SECTIONS 11 AND 12 OF THE CONTEMPT OF COURTS ACT,
1971, PRAYING TO ISSUE NOTICE CALLING UPON THE RESPONDENTS, WHY THEY SHOULD NOT BE DEALT WITH UNDER THE CONTEMPT OF COURTS ACT 1971, HAVING DISOBEYED THE ORDER / DIRECTION PASSED BY THE LEARNED SINGLE JUDGE OF THIS COURT IN WRIT PETITION NO.202747/2022 DATED 28.10.2022 AND PUNISH THE RESPONDENTS AS PER LAW, TO MEET ENDS OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY,
B.M. SHYAM PRASAD J., MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The complainant had filed the writ petition in W.P.No.202747/2022 contending that his representation dated 27.01.2021 with the sixth respondent for exclusion of his land from the proposed acquisition has not been considered, and the writ Court has disposed of the writ petition on 28.10.2022 directing the third and sixth respondents to consider the petitioner's representation [Annexure-D].
After the writ Court's order dated 28.10.2022 as aforesaid, the final notification is issued for acquisition of a total extent of about 600 acres including the complainant's land.

Therefore, the sixth respondent has issued Endorsement dated 15.04.2023 adverting to the proceedings under Section 28(3) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 informing the petitioner that his land cannot be excluded from the acquisition proceedings.

There is a delay in issuing the aforesaid Endorsement, and in the affidavit filed today, the sixth respondent, who has issued the subject Endorsement, has detailed circumstances to explain the delay stating that she has utmost respect for the Court proceedings.
The bona fides and the reasons offered stand out and must be accepted closing these contempt proceedings.

At this stage, Sri K.M. Ghate, the learned counsel for the complainant, submits that the Endorsement reads that compensation has been fixed for the petitioner's land and that is incorrect.
Sri A.M. Nagaral, the learned counsel for the sixth respondent, joins in response to say that proceedings have been conducted under Section 29 of the aforesaid Act to understand consensus amongst the different landowners and wherever there is consensus on the compensation payable for acquisition, the necessary agreements have been closed.
He further submits that in cases as in the complainant's case, because there is no consensus, proceedings as contemplated under Section 29(3) and (4) of the said Act are underway.
With this submission being taken on record, the proceedings stand dropped.

Sd/-
JUDGE Sd/-
